paper.title: A minimax and asymptotically optimal algorithm for stochastic bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic K-armed bandit with one-dimensional canonical exponential family arms (bounded means, bounded variance)
unmapped: Variance bounded uniformly over the family by V, giving Pinsker-like inequality kl(mu,mu') >= (mu-mu')^2/(2V)
settings.definition_quote: Each arm is assumed to be a probability distribution of some canonical one-dimensional exponential family $\nu_{\theta}$ ... we suppose that each arm $\nu_\theta$ satisfies $\mu=b'(\theta)\in [\mu-,\mu+]\subset I$ ... there exists $V>0$ such that $\sup_{\mu\in I} b''( {b'}^{-1}(\mu))\leq V<+\infty$.

symbols.v_mom: uniform upper bound V on the variance within the exponential family
symbols.mu_plus: upper end of the known interval of means
symbols.mu_minus: lower end of the known interval of means

source.label: th:minimax_bound
source.quote: For any family $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying the assumptions detailed in Section~\ref{sec:settings}, and for any bandit model $\nu\in\mathcal{F}$, the expected regret of the kl-UC$\Bpp$ algorithm is upper-bounded as R_T\leq 76 \sqrt{ V K T}+(\mu^+-\mu^-)K\,.

results.notes: Regret defined as sum of gaps times expected pull counts (pseudo-regret). Paper also notes it applies to [0,1]-valued bandits with V=1/4.

bound.regime: sqrt(22 V K / T) <= delta_a <= (mu_star - mu_a)/3

symbols.kl: KL divergence of the exponential family expressed in means

source.label: th:asymptotic_bound
source.quote: For any bandit model $\nu\in\mathcal{F}$, for any suboptimal arm $a$ and any $\delta$ such that $\sqrt{22 V K / T}\leq \delta\leq(\mustar-\mu_a)/3$, \E[N_a(T)]\leq \frac{\log(T)}{\kl(\mu_a+\delta,\mu^\star-\delta)}+O(\loglog(T)/\delta^2) which implies the asymptotic optimality

results.notes: Bound on expected number of pulls of a suboptimal arm, not regret directly. Leading term has constant 1, only second term is O(.). Explicit version from proof: log T/kl + log((1+log^2(T/K))/K)/kl + (16e^2+2)2VK/delta^2 + 1. Choosing delta ~ (loglog T)^{-1/2} gives asymptotic optimality (Lai-Robbins).

cited_results.setting_description: Stochastic K-armed bandits in exponential family; uniformly efficient strategies; expected pulls of suboptimal arm
Minimax lower bound over the exponential-family bandit class F (adaptation of Theorem A.2)
